methodological_rigor.justification: The study uses a well-designed preclinical toolkit combining TCGA/cBioPortal queries, lentiviral EXO1 overexpression in two independent cell lines (HeLa and U2OS), a catalytically inactive D173A mutant as a critical specificity control, and orthogonal assays (BrdU alkaline/neutral comet, S1 nuclease DNA fiber combing, SIRF, PLA, immunofluorescence, viability). Epistasis experiments (MRE11 mirin inhibition and knockdown, ZRANB3/SMARCAL1 knockdowns, BRCA2 depletion) convincingly support the proposed mechanism. Statistics use Mann-Whitney for fiber/comet data and unpaired two-tailed t-tests for imaging assays with adequate n (>=60-100 per condition) and triplicate viability assays, but there is no multiplicity correction across many panels, no power calculation, no blinding statement, no confidence intervals, and rescue experiments with siRNA-resistant add-backs are not performed. The TCGA correlations (EXO1 vs genome alterations) lack formal correlation coefficients or multivariable adjustment in-text.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a mechanistic preclinical/cell-line study (HeLa, U2OS, breast cancer lines) with TCGA correlative analysis, mapping to Oxford LoE 5. Clinical relevance is plausible: authors propose EXO1 overexpression as a 'BRCAness' biomarker predicting cisplatin and olaparib sensitivity, which is an actionable translational hypothesis given the prevalence of EXO1 overexpression across tumor types. However, no patient-level validation, no PDX/in vivo models, and no clinical correlation with therapy response are provided, so the translational path is suggestive rather than demonstrated.

reporting_quality.justification: As a preclinical cell-based study with no animal work, strict ARRIVE applies only partially; there is no dedicated reporting-standard checklist cited, though the authors reference a 'Nature Portfolio Reporting Summary.' Methods are detailed for cell lines (ATCC catalog numbers), siRNA sequences, antibodies (catalog numbers), drug doses, and imaging/software versions, supporting reproducibility. Gaps include absence of explicit blinding, randomization, biological replicate counts for each imaging assay, sample-size justification, and authentication/mycoplasma statements. Data availability is addressed via repeated 'Source Data are provided as a Source Data file' statements for every figure, but no code repository or raw-image repository deposit is described in the extracted text.

novelty_literature.justification: The central claim — that EXO1 overexpression alone, in BRCA-proficient cells, is sufficient to drive nascent-strand degradation at both ssDNA gaps and reversed forks, recruit MRE11, generate DSBs, and induce cisplatin/PARPi sensitivity — extends the authors' prior work (refs 26, 39, 40) in BRCA-deficient settings into a new, more prevalent tumor context. The finding that EXO1 overexpression bypasses BRCA2-mediated fork protection and is epistatic with BRCA2 loss is mechanistically novel and reframes RAD51's role in fork protection. It is a meaningful extension rather than first-in-class, as EXO1 overexpression in cancer and EXO1-MRE11 cooperation were previously reported; novelty is guarded by the fact that much of the conceptual framework builds on the same group's published assays.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly organized with a logical flow from TCGA observation to mechanism to phenotype to therapeutic implication. Figure legends are thorough with assay schematics, n values, median markers, and statistical annotations. Prose is precise and accessible; the discussion integrates findings with the BRCAness framework coherently. Minor issues include dense methods paragraphs, reliance on supplementary figures for key TCGA data, and occasional redundancy between abstract, introduction, and discussion.

key_strengths: Rigorous use of a D173A catalytic-dead EXO1 control across all mechanistic assays, strongly supporting specificity of the exonuclease activity
Convergent evidence from orthogonal assays (comet, S1 fiber combing, SIRF, PLA, gammaH2AX, viability) in two independent cell backgrounds (HeLa and U2OS)
Clear epistasis with BRCA2, MRE11 (mirin and siRNA), ZRANB3, and SMARCAL1 establishing the fork-reversal/MRE11 axis
Translationally relevant link: EXO1 overexpression phenocopies BRCAness including olaparib sensitivity comparable to BRCA2-KO cells
TCGA-based rationale spanning multiple tumor types (breast, hepatobiliary, melanoma, testicular, cervical) and correlation with structural genome alterations
key_concerns: No in vivo or patient-sample validation; clinical biomarker claim remains hypothesis-generating
TCGA correlations lack formal statistical reporting (no coefficients, CIs, or multivariable adjustment) in the extracted text
No blinding, randomization, sample-size justification, or multiplicity correction reported across many parallel comparisons
Rescue experiments with siRNA-resistant wild-type vs D173A EXO1 add-backs, and direct measurement of EXO1 protein/activity stoichiometry versus MRE11, are absent
Data availability limited to per-figure Source Data; no raw imaging data repository or analysis code deposited as described
chief_reviewer.rationale: Mechanistically convincing, well-controlled preclinical study with clear BRCAness translational framing and prior-work continuity; strong enough for a tier-2 venue (e.g., Nature Communications-level oncology/molecular biology) with minor revisions addressing statistical reporting of TCGA analyses and clinical-validation caveats.
